thread:
Nia H: Quick brainstorm — headline for the benchmark launch. I'm thinking "Predictable SLAs, predictable spend". We need a simple visual and one clear customer example.
Carlos V: Love the headline. Keep visuals two-up: left = latency distribution (not just p50), right = $/1k tokens with configuration callouts.
Hannah T: Add a tiny decision guide: when to use fastpath vs low-cost path. One sentence, non-technical.
Jules P: I'll draft the example vignette. How about: "Customer reduced 99.9th percentile latency from ~1.2s to 340ms and cut token cost by 27% using routing + quantization" — anonymized and round numbers.
Nia H: That reads well. Can we get empirical numbers for the visual? Carlos, any bench slice we can use?
Carlos V: Pasted a small sample from latest run (prod-like mix):
```
config,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,p999_ms,usd_per_1k
redwood-fast-q8,45,130,280,340,0.31
redwood-balanced-fp16,60,170,410,680,0.48
redwood-batch-quant,120,340,600,1200,0.13
```
Hannah T: Nice spread. For the copy: lead with problem -> solution -> proof -> CTA. Eg: "Averages hide the slow requests that cost you customers and money. Redwood's routing and model profiles tighten the tail and lower unit costs. Join our webinar for the deep-dive."
Jules P: CTA line: "Webinar: Benchmarks that map to real SLAs + live Q&A". DevRelBot: registration -> https://redwood.ai/webinar-slas (auto-post) :calendar:
Carlos V: Designer notes: use linear x-axis up to 2000ms, mark p99 and p999. Use short labels: Fast (Q8), Balanced (FP16), Batch (Quant). Right panel: bars with small callouts for batching/quant savings and a tiny legend for cost components.
Nia H: Also include one micro-flow: Request -> Fastpath (interactive) OR Slowpath (batch/cheap). One-line caption: "Pick the path that aligns with your SLA + unit economics."
Hannah T: Can we include an ops reproducibility note: bench commit SHA + dataset slice? Carlos please paste SHA.
Carlos V: Commit: be4f2c9. Dataset: mixed-chat-2026-02. I'll attach CSV in the ops thread.
Jules P: Action items: Jules to draft post + hero visual copy by EOD tomorrow; Hannah to write webinar email sequence; Carlos to confirm design assets and post SHA+CSV; Nia to review and finalize the three-slide hero.
Nia H: Sounds good. If anyone wants different headline variants, say now. Otherwise I'll queue this for design. :+1:
Carlos V: no changes from ops side.
DevRelBot: outreach-list created -> https://redwood.ai/track/webinar-slas (auto) :white_check_mark:
Jules P: I'll also prepare a 1-page cheat sheet (routing choices + quick config snippets) for download during the webinar.
Hannah T: Great — that will help with inbound nurture.
